lead.headline: Oʻahu homeowners have until September 30 to file for a home exemption
lead.summary: The City and County of Honolulu says eligible owner-occupants should file by September 30 for a home exemption effective July 1, 2027.
lead.why_it_matters: A qualifying exemption reduces the net taxable value of a principal residence by $140,000, or $180,000 when the owner is age 65 or older.
body: Oʻahu homeowners who use their property as their principal residence have until September 30, 2026, to file a home-exemption claim for the 2027–2028 tax year, according to the City and County of Honolulu.

The exemption reduces a qualifying home’s net taxable value by $140,000 for owners under age 65, or when no birth date is on file. Owners age 65 or older may qualify for a $180,000 exemption; eligibility is based on age as of June 30 before the tax year.
The property must be the owner’s principal home. The city says owners who already receive an exemption generally do not need to reapply unless ownership or use of the property has changed.

Approved claims filed by the September 30 deadline take effect July 1, 2027. Filing does not by itself determine a final tax bill, and owners should review the official eligibility requirements before submitting.

Claims may be filed online through the Real Property Assessment Division website at realproperty.honolulu.gov. Homeowners who need help can contact RPAD at (808) 768-3799 or use the contact information on the official city notice.

stories.headline: New Kailua DMV kiosk offers vehicle-registration renewals during store hours
stories.summary: A new self-service kiosk inside Foodland at Kailua Town Center expands Oʻahu’s DMV Now network to 11 locations.
stories.why_it_matters: Windward residents can renew eligible vehicle registrations during grocery-store hours, including evenings and weekends, without visiting a satellite city hall.
body: A new self-service vehicle-registration kiosk is now available inside Foodland at Kailua Town Center, 108 Hekili Street, according to the City and County of Honolulu.

The addition brings the DMV Now network to 11 kiosks across Oʻahu. The Kailua machine is available during the store’s operating hours, giving Windward residents an option for eligible renewals during evenings and weekends.

The city says customers can renew a vehicle registration at a kiosk up to 10 months after it expires, provided the vehicle has a current safety inspection. A standard $16 late fee applies to an expired registration.

Kiosk transactions include a $4 remote-transaction fee plus a 2.5% credit- or debit-card fee. Drivers should compare those charges with other renewal methods and bring the required renewal information.

The kiosk is intended for routine eligible renewals and does not replace every DMV service. Residents should consult the official city notice or AlohaQ/DMV resources when a transaction involves a title, ownership change or another service that requires staff assistance.
